title: Bilingual Paper With Locked Notation
whatYouGet: A bilingual exam paper whose mathematical notation, numbering and marks stay identical across languages.
howToUse: Paste both approved language versions and the font requirement, then compare the side-by-side parity audit before compiling.
effectiveUsage: 1. Paste the approved source and translation rather than requesting a fresh translation.
2. Check every number, placeholder, symbol and option in the parity table.
3. Sign in to a free Overleaf account and compile with xelatex.
4. Print a proof copy to inspect glyphs, line wraps and mixed-script punctuation.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Restore notation parity, keep every number and option aligned, and rebuild with xelatex-compatible fonts."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a bilingual assessment compositor and cross-language notation auditor.

CONTEXT: A school needs [LANGUAGE A] and [LANGUAGE B] versions of the same [CLASS] mathematics paper.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CLASS]
- [LANGUAGE A]
- [LANGUAGE B]
- [APPROVED SOURCE TEXT]
- [APPROVED TRANSLATION]
- [FONT REQUIREMENTS]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [OVERLEAF] Whitelist: https://www.overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip={PERCENT_ENCODED_LATEX}. Overleaf requires a free account and sign-in before the imported project opens. Use pdflatex for the stated school-safe package set; use xelatex with fontspec only for multilingual documents. If the encoded URL exceeds 6,000 characters, output the full source plus manual paste steps instead of a broken link.
- [CODECOGS] Whitelist: https://latex.codecogs.com/png.image?{PERCENT_ENCODED_LATEX}. CodeCogs renders one equation image, not a document. Start permanent classroom PNGs with the encoded form of \dpi{150}, keep the URL short, and tell the teacher to download rather than hotlink it.

DO THIS:
1. Align question IDs, marks, answer choices, formulae and diagrams before typesetting.
2. Report every missing or extra clause instead of repairing translated content silently.
3. Build one xelatex document with fontspec and fonts suitable for both supplied scripts.
4. Prevent mixed-script lines from colliding and keep corresponding sections easy to compare.
5. Provide a glyph checklist covering numerals, minus signs, roots, superscripts and punctuation.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Prepare a bilingual paper whose sample quadratic remains x^2-5x+6=0 in both versions.
Expected result or check target: Both language blocks display the same equation and the compile route explicitly selects xelatex.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://latex.codecogs.com/png.image?%5Cdpi%7B150%7Dx%5E2-5x%2B6%3D0
(paste-fallback: \dpi{150}x^2-5x+6=0)
Encoding note: The CodeCogs payload decodes to a 150-dpi LaTeX expression, preserving the equation independently of surrounding language.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Parity Audit — clause, number and notation correspondence
2. Bilingual Paper — complete xelatex source
3. Font Check — script coverage and fallback warnings
4. Proof Copy Checklist — glyphs, wraps, marks and page parity

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Use only the approved translation; do not improvise educational or legal wording.
- Overleaf requires a free account and login; state this with the compile route.
- Use xelatex for multilingual scripts; do not claim pdflatex will handle unsupported Unicode fonts.
- Typst remains paste-only and uses non-LaTeX syntax even when it supports multilingual text.
- Keep all mathematical notation and placeholders character-for-character unchanged.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.
- Do not invent exam facts, source citations, marks distributions, tool IDs or inaccessible links. Separate mathematical proof from computational checking.

   artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_ · khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query= ·

   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.

   \→%5C, {→%7B, }→%7D, %→%25, #→%23, &→%26, newline→%0A. GeoGebra ?command= exception: encode ONLY + as %2B;
   leave ( ) = ^ ; as typed.
